questions.question: How does the civilian population become the battlefield in the state vs. non-state asymmetric warfare? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• In state vs. non-state asymmetric warfare, the civilian population is the battlefield-When the
  • professional army cannot distinguish between a combatant and a civilian, the spatial boundaries of
  • war dissolve. - The conflict enters everyday spaces-markets, hospitals, and homes-becoming a
  • general social condition. - Guerrillas, insurgents, and terrorists do not wear uniforms or operate
  • from distinct military bases. They are deeply embedded within the populace CO1
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: How does the ‘homecoming’ become a redeployment in the story? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• In Phil Klay’s Redeployment- returning home from a war zone does not signify a true return to
  • peace or normalcy- conditioned by hyper-vigilance, trauma, and the rules of engagement of the
  • battlefield-treating everyday life like an ongoing theatre of war. CO2
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: "Rifle was not merely a weapon; it was an extension of his body". Explain with reference to "Redeployment" / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• In military contexts, survival relies on an absolute, instinctive symbiosis between the soldier and
  • their weapon. The rifle ceases to be an external tool and becomes a vital sensory organ-totalizing
  • modern warfare is—shaping not just the soldier's ideology, but their physical posture and
  • psychological identity, making it difficult to shed the military identity. CO2
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: What is the significance of the kite and tail in the poem "If I must die"? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Refaat Alareer's poem- the kite represents childhood, innocence, play, and the soaring aspiration of
  • human freedom-The tail of the kite signifies connection, balance, and the transmission of hope
  • across generations. By mentioning a child who looks up to see the kite, the poem emphasizes that
  • hope is never lost. CO2

questions.question: Why did the narrator not believe Mags in "There's a hole in the city" ? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Mags is the narrator's Friend-New York City in the immediate aftermath of the September 11
  • attacks, the narrator believes Mags is suffering from intense psychological distress caused by the
  • catastrophe. When she claims that the attacks ripped open a rift in urban spacetime allowing
  • historical ghosts to return-he dismisses her accounts as grief-fueled hallucinations. CO3

questions.question: What does the "bullet hole" symbolize in the context of the poem, "Telemachus"? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• The poem alludes to the Greek myth of Odysseus and his son Telemachus, Vuong overlays this
  • mythic framework with the historical trauma of the Vietnam War and the refugee experience. The
  • bullet hole symbolizes the physical and psychological violence of war that has permanently marked,
  • and ultimately broken, the father. CO3
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Mrs. Pirelli did not come home from the hospital, but went to live with her son in Connecticut. Who is being described here from the story “There's a hole in the city"? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• On the morning of the Sept 11 attacks, Mrs. Pirelli suffered a heart attack while watching the smoke
  • and flames on television. Because her son worked in the World Trade Center, she was immediately
  • consumed by the terrifying belief that he had burned to death- The rescue team transported her to
  • St. Vincent’s Hospital in the fire chief's personal car- her son survived. CO3

questions.question: "Modern conflict is no longer defined by strict territorial boundaries or clear military endpoints, but by permanent structural inequalities and ideological struggles." Explain. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Traditional wars have clear end dates, but an ideological conflict lacks a logical stopping point
  • because the "enemy" is an abstract concept -Society remains in a perpetual state of readiness,
  • blurring the line between peacetime and wartime. CO1

questions.question: War Machines and Heteronomy. Discuss with reference to the essay "Necropolitics". / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Achille Mbembe expands upon Michel Foucault’s concept of biopower-the state’s power to "foster
  • life or disallow it to the point of death"-by shifting the analytical focus directly toward necropower-
  • the sovereign power to dictate who may live and who must die-The war machine reduces human
  • bodies to disposable entities, enforcing total subjugation, transforming citizens into targets, and
  • turning entire regions into spaces where destruction is normalized and self-determination is
  • completely erased. CO2

questions.question: Childhood in conflict zones-constant state of physical pain and fear. How does the father try to create memories for his son in "Sea prayer"? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• In Khaled Hosseini’s illustrated poem Sea Prayer, the young boy, Marwan, has known a childhood
  • defined entirely by the Syrian civil war-to shield his son from the absolute terror of the present and
  • the perilous sea crossing ahead, the father uses the act of memory-keeping as an emotional
  • sanctuary. CO3

questions.question: Discuss the role of memory and forgetting in "The End and the Beginning." / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• In Wisława Szymborska’s masterwork "The End and the Beginning," memory and forgetting act as
  • a necessary, interlocking mechanism for human survival. Szymborska presents a profound paradox:
  • while forgetting is a betrayal of the past and a historical danger, it is simultaneously the only
  • psychological engine that allows humanity to heal, rebuild, and move forward after massive trauma.
  • CO4
